scope: Contextual paper-counting units in Nepal and their relation to Hodgson's 1843 Wallich paper bill.
central_claim: Dhep/ढेप is securely a Nepalese handmade-paper bundle/count term, but its reported numerical depth is context-dependent. A ten-sheet convention is strongly documented in traditional/lexical sources; a twenty-sheet dhep is directly documented by 1998-99 field observation in Myagdi-Parbat-Baglung; a 2013 NAST synthesis directly prints 200 sheets per dhep but is secondary for production practice and may conflate dhep with the independently documented 200-sheet kori level. Do not store a single universal sheet-equivalent for dhep.

attested_values.date_of_practice: late twentieth-century description of traditional practice
attested_values.source: Bhupahari Paudel, Ancient Nepal no.103, p.33
corroboration: modern Nepali lexical definition: ढेप = ten tau of Nepali paper
Nepali-English dictionary tradition: dhepa = ten sheets of Nepalese paper

attested_values.source: Griha Man Singh, Ancient Nepal no.144, p.16
attested_values.physical_bundle_method: twenty dried sheets tied into a single bundle with thin bast strips

attested_values.locality: national synthesis / exact production locality unresolved

units.control: Do not assume 20 western-Nepal dhep bundles necessarily compose the same numerical kori relation without local evidence.

hodgson_1843_bill.catalogue_rates: Rupees 10/- and 14/- per bundle as prose-transcribed

data_model.rule: Metrological value is a contextual attribute of an attestation, not a universal property of a lexeme.

source_control_rules: Retain dhep as securely identified Nepalese handmade-paper vocabulary.
Do not assign a universal numerical value to dhep.
Treat ten sheets as a strong convention; treat twenty sheets as direct western-Nepal field evidence.
Preserve the NAST 200-sheet statement exactly while marking possible unit conflation with kori.
Do not use a dictionary definition to override locality-specific workshop observation.
Keep catalogue transcription, normalized lexeme, reported package depth, and historian normalization separate.
Do not normalize Hodgson f.117 to total sheets before the original account layout is inspected.
